body.statement: What is the sharp local envelope of \(\omega^{\star}(\delta)-\omega^{\star}(0)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), and which observable prefix-Gram restrictions identify subclasses on which the restricted modulus vanishes? Use the annulus decomposition of \(\psi_{n,k}-\psi_{n,l}\) and the explicit tied-risk witness to derive matching upper and lower bounds without imposing an oracle restriction on candidate bias.
body.justification: The counterexample settles the global exact-tie question negatively but leaves the sharp excess modulus and the largest empirically meaningful benign-tie subclass open.
body.gap: No located paper gives a risk-to-target modulus for generated external-control prefixes or a prefix-Gram restriction that restores tie invariance.
body.consumer: The sharp envelope determines how much a localized confidence interval must widen beyond its unavoidable exact-tie width.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine the exact class-wide right-hand envelope of \(\omega^{\star}(\delta)-\omega^{\star}(0)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), including a matching legal lower construction.
obligation.obstruction: The legal class has no Gram coercivity or compactness condition connecting squared-norm differences to Hilbert-coordinate distance.  The finite-support witness proves a positive exact-tie width, while the polarization identity alone gives no rate for the excess above the unknown global supremum at zero.
obligation.attempted: Used the annulus perturbation calculation, the polarization identity, and the explicit tied-risk family.  These prove a computable sufficient subclass restriction but do not determine whether the full-class supremum is right-continuous, has a jump, or is already saturated at exact ties.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\), define its restricted modulus by replacing \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) with \(\mathcal A\), and define the observable prefix Gram coordinate
\[
 g_n(k,l)=\langle h_{n,k},h_{n,l}\rangle_n
 =\beta_{n,k}\beta_{n,l}+\Gamma_n(k,l).
\]
Then
\[
 d_n(k,l)^2=\rho_{n,k}+\rho_{n,l}-2g_n(k,l),
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,k}-\rho_{n,l}
 =\langle h_{n,k}+h_{n,l},h_{n,k}-h_{n,l}\rangle_n. \tag{A}
\]
Consequently, if a subclass satisfies the computable Gram-coercivity restriction
\[
 |\rho_{n,k}-\rho_{n,l}|\geq\kappa d_n(k,l)^\gamma
 \quad\text{for every }n,k,l
\]
for fixed \(\kappa>0\) and \(\gamma>0\), then its restricted modulus obeys the sharp deterministic implication
\[
 \omega_{\mathcal A}^{\star}(\delta)\leq(\delta/\kappa)^{1/\gamma},
\]
and hence vanishes at zero.  Both sides of the restriction are computed from \((\beta_{n,k},\Gamma_n(k,l))\) through (A).  Conversely, the proved finite-support witness has \(|\rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}-\rho_{n,0}|=0\) and \(d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)\to\sqrt{D_\infty}>0\), so no positive \((\kappa,\gamma)\) coercivity inequality can hold on the full legal class, and \(\omega^{\star}(0)\geq\sqrt{D_\infty}\).
